source_caption:
Shooter — Betrayal, Revenge & Survival

Shooter (2007) follows Bob Lee Swagger, a highly skilled former Marine sniper who lives in isolation after a mission ends in tragedy. Known for his precision, patience, and ability to operate under extreme pressure, Swagger wants nothing more than to stay away from the world he once served.

His quiet life comes to an end when government officials recruit him to help prevent an assassination attempt. Using his military expertise, Swagger studies the situation and provides advice on how the attack might happen. However, the mission turns into a deadly setup when he is framed for the assassination of a high-profile political figure.

With the authorities hunting him and powerful people working to silence him, Swagger must use his skills to uncover the conspiracy and prove his innocence. As he searches for the truth, he discovers that the betrayal goes much deeper than he ever imagined.

The film explores themes of loyalty, corruption, justice, betrayal, and survival. It shows how a man trained to serve his country can become its target when powerful individuals decide he knows too much.

What makes Shooter compelling is watching Swagger use his patience, intelligence, and unmatched marksmanship to outmaneuver the people who framed him and expose the truth.

💬 They framed the wrong man—and now he's coming for everyone who betrayed him.

source_details.synopsis: Shooter is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Jonathan Lemkin, based on the 1993 novel Point of Impact by Stephen Hunter. The film follows Force Recon Marine Scout Sniper veteran Bob Lee Swagger (Mark Wahlberg), who is framed for murder by a mercenary unit operating for a private military firm. The film also stars Michael Peña, Danny Glover, Kate Mara, Levon Helm, and Ned Beatty. Shooter was produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura through di Bonaventura Pictures, and released by Paramount Pictures in the United States on March 23, 2007. The film received mixed reviews and grossed $95.7 million on a $61 million budget.
